summary.name: Hubzilla
summary.one_liner: Hubzilla is a decentralised, open source communication server that combines social networking, cloud storage, blogging, forums, and content management under one privacy permission system.
use_cases: Run a private or public social network for a community
Share posts and files with selected people or channels
Host a blog or forum on your own server
Self-host cloud storage alongside social features
Publish content across channels on different servers
Back up and migrate your connections and content
summary.what_it_does: Hubzilla is a general purpose communication server that integrates social networking, cloud storage, blog and forum features, and content management into one system. Everything published can be restricted to chosen channels and people, with permissions that work across channels on different servers or other communication services. The page says it includes built-in migration and live backups of connections, settings, and published content. It is described as completely decentralised and open source, with plugins, themes, and many configuration options for customization.
notable: Decentralised permission system that applies across servers and other communication services
Integrates social network, cloud storage, blog/forum, and CMS features in one platform
Built-in migration and live backups of connections, settings, and content
Extensible via plugins and themes; MIT licensed per the awesome-selfhosted listing
caveats: Page text does not describe hardware or hosting requirements beyond the PHP listing
Decentralised permissions behaviour across other services is described only at a high level
